1: Central review needs a final disposition for Stardust.
Disposition. It sounds like a word someone uses when they don't want to say closing.
Before anyone closes anything, tell them the bracket is still temporary.
I intend to. That part of the station remains unusually eloquent.
2: Option one makes us a material pilot with an output quota.
Option two keeps us operating until the pilot money disappears. Lovely choices.
Option three closes the station. There isn't a fourth box.
Then we'll have to write one. That's the work now.
3: This repair works with the ordinary brace. The sample helps fill one gap. It isn't a new station function.
It's still an interesting physical result. You don't have to make it sound embarrassed.
Can we test how often this would replace a real part?
Not honestly, no. I wouldn't bet a building on it. I might bet a spare washer.
4: They've given us three options and none is the place I manage.
Then put operations on one side and the material on the other. Don't make them sound like the same job.
I have notes on the station's persistent mysteries.
Start with the repair records. They're much less mysterious.
5: I've collected the ordinary maintenance history and response records.
How much of this looks like the last year?
All of it. Most of it was inconvenient when it happened.
And some of the inconvenient days gave us the samples.
Don't let that be a reason to schedule more inconvenient days.
We tried that. I still owe Dock Two an apology.
6: Here's the repaired bracket, the failed checks, and the work we did around the delay.
But it's actual evidence. We had a problem, tested options, and kept the station working.
And occasionally complained with great skill. Please include that under local expertise.
7: This sample held twice and failed when we changed the temperature. I'm not hiding either result.
Of course I do. Some of my favorite things are questions we haven't answered.
Then our report should leave you room to keep asking, without promising the answers in advance.
8: This is where the conveyor blocked the dock when we moved a service job early.
I know. I just wanted to be sure the report remembers it too.
It will. And when the next ship comes in, I'll listen when you tell me what the schedule means.
9: They want an owner, task, condition and chain of custody. That much we can record.
And they don't need a field for what someone was thinking while it happened.
I'm leaving a blank for context that people actually choose to share.
Can we also leave it empty if nobody chooses?
Yes. I had to sit with that idea for a while, but yes.
Behavioral context: not required. I rather like writing that.
10: This packet has the station's work history on one side and the material tests on the other.
Good. Now nobody can confuse a sample with a replacement bracket.
They're still going to ask whether we can make more.
Then we tell them we don't know. I think we've earned the right to be boring.
You can be boring. Mira and I have interesting repairs to finish.
11: Primary function: operating and maintaining Stardust. Secondary observation: collecting and testing incidental material.
Say the material can be useful under tested conditions. Not that it always will be.
And no one has to perform an emotion to make the pilot work.
The two parts of the report now agree with the work history.
12: I read the fourth option. It's unlike the categories central offered.
I know. But it's the station you've visited.
You'll have to explain why operations deserve the budget without a promised material output.
I'm planning to explain the same thing we showed you in the corridor.
13: Option one offers faster parts and a larger material budget.
And we'd be expected to produce a quantity we can't predict.
Correct. Option four gives you a defensible operating budget, but fewer guarantees.
I know why the faster route is tempting.
So do I. We tried moving our jobs around a target once.
14: Which option are you asking me to recommend?
The fourth. The station we actually run, not a factory we hope to become.
I can take it forward. I can't promise it'll win.
I wouldn't trust you if you could.
15: Central has returned questions. They're not quite ready to reject this.
Reproducible output? The work record. Repairs, response times, service kept running.
And what material yield can you promise?
None. We have a physical observation, with limits. You can't schedule it.
Then why keep observing it? Mira, that's your question.
Because sometimes science is worth doing before anyone knows what to buy from it.
16: They want one statement of value. I'm trying not to write it like a conference banner.
We keep the place working. That's what people call us for.
And we test the unusual things we find without pretending they know how we feel.
And people can still be people when they aren't being measured.
17: Are you declining the dedicated-material option? It would be easier to defend.
Easier for the report. Harder for every person who has to work here. That's my answer.
18: The decision hasn't arrived. The bracket has still arrived zero times.
I can check the monitoring interval. It's better than standing around refreshing a screen.
I'll take the next work order.
Good. We had a station before they made a category for us.
19: Still holding. And the replacement still hasn't appeared.
You might miss the pleasure of being annoyed with procurement.
The material filler remains unchanged. I wish I had something new to tell you.
Safety record closed. Nobody's asked me to describe the emotional conditions.
I put the quiet-room chairs back. Someone borrowed both of them.
Astra, ordinary service order. It isn't waiting for central's answer.
20: Central review has returned its decision.
Adaptive operations approved. Incidental material observation retained. No output target.
Does 'active' come with an actual bracket?
21: Replacement part due in two days.
Do not investigate the one good thing procurement has done for us.
What are we supposed to do with a permanent part? We've become attached to temporary.
I can show you the difference in the maintenance register.
22: Behavioral context: not required. I never expected a form to make me feel so free.
You're coming over tonight, aren't you? Everybody's playing. Pixa too.
I'm bringing the cards. Your set has the wrong scoring instructions.
You'd enjoy the game if you stopped treating the scores like evidence.
The vending machine has printed our station approval. A curious witness.
Normal enough. And for once, Glorp, knock on the door when you get there.
